entries.grounds: mutant_view confirms RecursionError is dropped from the :517 except tuple. The size-cap-before-json.loads argument holds: cap = _RESULT_FLOOR + 8*sum(len(rel)+8) (:505), ~65640 bytes for a one-file request; the size check `size>cap -> BAD_RESULT` (:512-514) runs before `json.loads` (:516). Re-measured the RecursionError threshold on this interpreter (python3 -P -B): json.loads('['*n+']'*n) PARSES at n=30000(60KB)/50000(100KB)/100000(200KB) and first raises RecursionError at n=150000 (300KB). So the smallest RecursionError-triggering payload (~250-300KB) exceeds the one-file cap (~65KB) by ~4-5x; for a multi-file request you would need thousands of files, and the real GREP_WORKER (:382-408) emits depth<=3 JSON. The dropped branch is unreachable for any realistic request. Ran tests.v2.test_v21_fa_grep_worker on the mutant: PASS (survives); baseline PASS. entries.grounds: The author's REFUTED is CORRECT and the refutation is REPRODUCED. mutant_view confirms :432 `skipped != sorted(set(skipped))` -> `skipped != list(set(skipped))`. Measured set-iteration order on this interpreter (python3 -P -B): list(set([7,8]))==[8,7] != sorted(set([7,8]))==[7,8] (they DIFFER), whereas list(set([2,1]))==[1,2]==sorted(set([2,1])) (the existing 'skipped out of order' case [2,1] does NOT distinguish the two, which is why the mutant survives). Ran _worker_facts directly from a COPY tree, original vs mutant, rels of length 9: ORIGINAL -> skipped_binary=[7,8] returns {'present':True,...,'skipped_binary':['f7.py','f8.py']} (accepted) and [8,7] raises WorkerFailed('BAD_RESULT'); MUTANT -> [7,8] raises WorkerFailed('BAD_RESULT') (WRONGLY REJECTS a valid ascending result) and [8,7] returns {...'skipped_binary':['f8.py','f7.py']} (WRONGLY ACCEPTS a non-ascending result). This is product-reachable: the real GREP_WORKER appends binary-file indexes in ascending iteration order, so a repository with binary (NUL) files at indexes 7 and 8 among >=9 files sent yields [7,8], which the mutant turns into a BAD_RESULT -> HARNESS_FAILED.
